experiments.hypothesis: For every returned pair the two messages are distinct and their complete 3-round digests agree in the low 18 bits (digest bytes 0 and 1 and the low 2 bits of byte 2). This is exact: the program recovers a merge of two trails of the chain x -> low 18 bits of the digest of P || 0^32 || x. The number of trials that return a pair is the number of single attempts that succeeded; expected about 0.66 of the trials (the program's own run gave 163 of 256), and equal to the ideal-function control within sampling error (two-proportion |z| below 3.5 expected). Observations (untrusted, the program's own): target_ok, ideal_ok, batches, halts, t1_steps (mean about sqrt(pi 2^12 / 2) = 80.2). Not shown: any width-256 cost or success probability.
experiments.probability_inference: none: participant program may couple trials, ignore seeds or replay pairs; frequency is not an iid success-probability estimate

reproducibility.scope: Two fresh isolated executions only; not a proof for all future runs or seeds.

experiments.scope: The blake3-r3-prefix-v1 target, collision of the low 18 bits of the complete digest. Each trial runs ONE attempt of the shipped 256-lane search (plan(18): distinguished points with the low 2 bits zero, 8 batches of 256 lanes, cut rule, table, recovery on the packed circuit) from a word derived from the trial seed, with no amplification, and returns the two 128-byte messages P || 0^32 || x and P || 0^32 || y (P the prefix of proof.md Section 8) when the attempt found a pair, two nulls otherwise. The same program also runs the same attempt on an ideal function of the same width (keyed blake2b) and one family-law run with a fresh key at n = 12; these are reported as untrusted observations only.
experiments.scope_limit: Only the selected-target output event on returned pairs was checked. Internal predicates, algorithmic work, extrapolation and expected cost remain unverified.

experiments.hypothesis: For every returned pair the two messages P || 0^32 || x and P || 0^32 || y are distinct and their complete 3-round digests agree in the low 21 bits (digest bytes 0 and 1 and the low 5 bits of byte 2). This is exact. If f is uniform on the points sampled, a trial returns a pair with probability 1 - exp(-C(2048, 2) / 2^21) = 0.632 (expected about 162 of 256 trials; the program's own run gave 170 of 256), and each projection has mean 0.9995 equal pairs per trial. Observations (untrusted): source, dup_w0, dup_w3, dup_w7, dup_xor8, dup_sum8, dup_p01, dup_p23. Not shown: collision structure at 2^128 evaluations.

experiments.scope: The blake3-r3-prefix-v1 target with the fixed first block P at full width 256, with the key m0..m7 of the last block = 0. Each trial evaluates 2048 points x with the shipped bit-sliced circuit (source by trial index mod 3: uniform inputs from the seed, counter inputs r + i, iterates of f from 256 seed-derived starts), and returns two distinct points whose complete digests agree in the low 21 bits when the set contains such a pair, two nulls otherwise. Untrusted observations: the numbers of equal pairs in seven 21-bit projections of the digest.
